review_context: Codex review of current thread instructions requesting deterministic DAD capture for hard issues, exceptions, and cross-repo workflow or asset discoveries.
finding_title: Hard issues and cross-repo workflow assets need deterministic DAD outbox capture across repos.
finding_summary: The user repeatedly directed that complex issues, exceptions, workflow discoveries, and combined cross-repo assets must be captured as candidate DAD mail with classification, evidence, assumptions, decision logic, fix rationale, and no hidden chain-of-thought.
observable_context: The current intake repo already has a candidate-only DAD review issue outbox recorder that appends to .digital-asset/mail/outbox.jsonl.
The user wants the same pattern enforced across all repos so hard issues and reusable workflow assets are not trapped in chat or one repo.
The user specifically called out cross-repo combined assets and partial assets discovered in one repo then reused in another as events DAD should see.
The boundary remains candidate mail only; DAD or human review must decide whether any pattern becomes reusable learning or an Exception Lake event class.
observable_decision_logic: If an agent discovers a hard issue, novel fix, exception pattern, or cross-repo workflow asset, a durable candidate mail record should be produced.
The mail record should carry issue classes, candidate exception labels, source repo, artifact refs, fix refs, test refs, observable decision logic, and promotion boundaries.
The mail record should explicitly exclude hidden chain-of-thought and raw private payloads.
DAD should classify recurring patterns before any cross-repo learning rule or Exception Lake event mapping is promoted.
solution_path: Use the intake DAD review issue outbox contract as a candidate reference implementation.
Ask DAD to define a cross-repo deterministic capture policy for hard issues, exceptions, workflow assets, and combined assets.
Add repo-local tests or hooks in each participating repo so candidate DAD mail is written before promotion or learning claims are made.
Map mail issue classes and candidate exception labels to DAD's future exception-lake classification strategy.
applies_when: An agent identifies a complex issue, exception, workflow asset, cross-repo dependency, or reusable fix pattern that should survive beyond chat.
A repo-local agent combines an external repo asset with local implementation work to create a new workflow artifact.
A human asks that DAD learn from a hard problem, exception pattern, or review output.
does_not_apply_when: The item is a routine typo with no reusable issue pattern.
The record would require raw private matter payloads, credentials, or hidden chain-of-thought to be useful.
The issue is already captured by a newer DAD mail record with the same issue id and version.
danger_if_misapplied: If this becomes silent learning instead of candidate mail, DAD could promote unreviewed chat conclusions across repos or admit misleading exception classes into the future Lake.
suggested_actions: DAD should classify this as a cross-repo governance and learning-loop candidate.
DAD should design a deterministic mail/outbox contract for issue, exception, workflow-asset, and combined-asset capture across repos.
DAD should define exception-lake event classes only after reviewing candidate mail patterns and owner boundaries.
reviewer_notes: This record is metadata-only and summarizes observable user instructions and repo behavior.
It intentionally excludes hidden chain-of-thought and raw private payloads.
The intake implementation is a reference, not cross-repo canon.
red_team_notes: Do not treat DAD mail as approved learning.
Do not let issue capture bypass repo owner review or Semantic Substrate authority.
Do not store private matter data or chain-of-thought in DAD mail.
